summary: SUVs, pickups and tractors are central Mahindra businesses, alongside lending and other group companies providing products and services.
description: Mahindra & Mahindra makes vehicles and farm equipment and supplies them through dealers and other sales routes. For example, a family may buy an SUV, while a farmer may buy a tractor to pull equipment for farm work. Group companies also lend money and carry out other activities; a vehicle sale and a loan earn in different ways.
money: The manufacturing businesses earn from vehicles, tractors, parts and related goods or services. They pay for components, workers, factories, transport and support. Lending businesses receive interest but must pay for their funding and allow for borrowers who fail to repay. Each activity has its own costs before group profit remains.
customers: Vehicle buyers, farmers, businesses using work vehicles, dealers and borrowers served by the finance business. Other group companies serve their own business or household customers.
drivers: Demand for vehicles and tractors, buyers’ incomes and access to loans, components and factory costs, borrower repayments and the money committed to new businesses.

groups.title: Vehicles
groups.examples: Thar, Scorpio and XUV ranges, pickups, commercial and electric vehicles.
groups.explanation: Families buy vehicles for travel; businesses may use them to carry people or goods for income. Their running costs, features and ability to afford repayments can differ.

groups.title: Tractors and farm equipment
groups.examples: Mahindra and Swaraj tractors, implements and farm machinery.
groups.explanation: A tractor supplies power to pull or operate equipment. Implements are tools used with it for farm tasks. Farmers consider expected farm income, the work needed and whether they can afford the purchase.

groups.title: Lending
groups.examples: Group loans to vehicle and rural borrowers.
groups.explanation: A borrower receives money and repays it with interest under the agreement. The lender needs its own funding and bears the risk of late or missing repayments. This is different from selling a tractor.

groups.title: Other group companies and investments
groups.examples: Examples in the annual review include Tech Mahindra’s computer services, property development, holiday resorts and a business that stores and transports goods for other companies.
groups.explanation: These can earn from different jobs, such as helping a business with computer systems or moving goods. A subsidiary is a controlled company; an associate is an investment accounted for differently. A shared group name does not mean every company’s full sales belong to the parent.

basics.title: A good SUV market is not the same as a good tractor market
basics.text: Family spending and new models can influence SUV demand. Crop prices, farm income, local rain and replacement needs influence tractors. Read both businesses separately before judging the group.

steps.title: Work out the customer’s need
steps.text: Choose vehicles and farm equipment for the jobs and budgets the business serves.

steps.title: Obtain components, build and check
steps.text: Arrange suppliers and factories, then manufacture and test the products. Missing parts or faults can stop supply.

steps.title: Supply buyers and provide support
steps.text: Dealers and other routes get products to users. Parts and repair services help keep vehicles and machines usable. If a group lender provides finance, it separately assesses and collects that loan.

steps.title: Receive cash and decide where to spend it
steps.text: Product payments must cover manufacturing and business costs; loan repayments must cover lending obligations. The group also decides what cash to commit to factories, new businesses and acquisitions.

specifics.title: Bookings still need to become cars customers take home
specifics.text: A popular launch must be followed by enough production, completed sales and reliable products. Buyers can cancel while waiting; faults can create repair costs afterwards.

specifics.title: Rain alone does not decide tractor demand
specifics.text: Local crop earnings, prices, borrowing and the need to replace old equipment also matter. Good national rainfall does not mean every farmer has more money to spend.

specifics.title: The group total combines different kinds of earnings
specifics.text: The accounts include manufacturing, lending and other businesses under the reporting rules. Transactions between group companies are removed, and some earnings belong to outside co-owners. Check these adjustments before treating every business line as money available to the parent.

watch: Do vehicle bookings become completed sales?
Orders are earlier than production, payment and customer handover.
Read completed sales, production limits, cancellations and expected repair costs together. A long waiting list is not a guarantee of future earnings.
Can farmers afford the tractors they need?
Farm spending depends on local and seasonal conditions.
Read tractor demand alongside crop earnings, loan availability and replacement needs. Separate Indian and export sales where available.
Are electric-vehicle investments finding enough buyers?
Developing and making vehicles costs money before demand is proven.
Follow which company makes the investment, when production starts, actual sales and funding needs. Do not substitute a target for an achieved result.
Are borrowers repaying the finance business?
A larger loan balance can include more unpaid loans.
Read late payments, collections and amounts set aside for expected loan losses. Check the lender’s funding costs separately from vehicle manufacturing costs.
Are different businesses earning enough for the money committed?
Several activities can need cash at the same time.
Read day-to-day cash generation, equipment spending, acquisitions and transfers between group companies. Compare each activity’s earnings with what it needs to keep operating or expand.
risks: Families, farmers and work-vehicle operators can cut spending for different reasons.
Factories or new models run into problems
Parts shortages, delays and faults can make strong customer interest hard to turn into sales.
Late or missing payments can reduce finance-business earnings and available cash.
Expansion and acquisitions can require funding before enough customers or earnings arrive.
context: November 2026: cars grew, tractors dipped for a season

Mahindra’s 5 November 2026 results for July–September 2026 show group profit up about a quarter from a year earlier. The vehicle business grew strongly, while tractor sales and farm profit fell. The company says the main reason for the farm fall was timing: the festival season, when many farmers buy, began in October this year but in September last year. Its 1 October 2026 sales release had already shown the same pattern for September. Compare longer periods and read the company’s explanation before treating one quarter’s fall as weaker farm demand.
sources: September 2026 vehicle and tractor sales releases · 1 October 2026

financialNotes.title: Internal revenue is not another outside sale
financialNotes.text: The existing table reports consolidated segments and deducts inter-segment revenue in its reconciliation. Segment results include the exceptional and associate/joint-venture effects stated in the source; they are not a uniform after-tax result for each product brand.

financialNotes.title: Finance costs require care
financialNotes.text: Lending has financing costs within its own business economics. Read the remaining group-level finance costs and unallocated items in the reconciliation rather than subtracting the same cost twice.

stepsTitle: From the factory to a vehicle at work.

quick.title: What it does
quick.text: Mahindra builds SUVs, pickup trucks and tractors in its own factories. The wider group also lends money to vehicle buyers and owns other companies, such as Tech Mahindra.

quick.title: Who pays
quick.text: Car buyers, farmers and businesses that use work vehicles, usually through dealers, who buy the vehicles from Mahindra. Borrowers pay interest to the group’s lending company.

quick.title: How it earns
quick.text: By selling vehicles, tractors, parts and related services. The lending business earns interest, which is a different kind of income with its own costs.

quick.title: What it spends on
quick.text: Components, workers, factories, transport and support. The lending business also pays for the money it lends and allows for borrowers who fail to repay.

helps.title: Different kinds of buyer
helps.text: Families buying SUVs, farmers buying tractors and businesses buying pickups face different pressures, so they need not all cut spending at once. In July–September 2026, for example, vehicle sales grew while tractor sales fell.

helps.title: Leading positions
helps.text: Mahindra sells more tractors than any other company in India and has the largest share of SUV sales by value, its results say.

helps.title: Its own finance business
helps.text: Mahindra’s annual report says a large share of vehicle purchases are paid for with loans. Its group company Mahindra Finance lends to vehicle and rural buyers, which helps those buyers get credit.

hurts.title: Tractor demand follows the rains
hurts.text: Mahindra’s FY 2025–26 annual report says tractor demand and rural spending are linked to the monsoon. A weak rainy season lowers farm incomes, so farmers may delay buying a tractor, though the report says these swings have become smaller.

hurts.title: Dearer loans slow sales
hurts.text: Because many vehicles are bought on credit, the annual report says affordable loans are key to demand. When interest rates rise or lenders become stricter, fewer buyers can afford a vehicle.

hurts.title: Raw-material and currency swings
hurts.text: The annual report says sharp moves in the prices of steel, aluminium, oil-based materials and currencies can squeeze its margins. In July–September 2026 its vehicle and tractor margins were lower than a year earlier.

hurts.title: Borrowers fail to repay
hurts.text: Mahindra Finance lends to many rural and small-business borrowers. When their incomes fall, more loans go unpaid, which reduces the finance business’s earnings and cash.
